summary: Phase-2 inbound rollback bug fix verified at unit-test level. Ran the ebms-orchestrator Maven test suite; every non-Testcontainers test passes (34/34). Key results: OrchestratorServiceAntiSpoofingTest 4/4 (all four contract scenarios of the new InboundMessageTrackingService: OIN-match happy path invokes persistReceived+markProcessing and never persistFailed; OIN-mismatch invokes trackingService.persistFailed with error detail containing the spoofed OIN, throws SecurityFailure, and blocks all downstream CPA/crypto/persistReceived calls; blank OIN with enforce=true invokes persistFailed with error detail mentioning X-Forwarded-Client-OIN; blank OIN with enforce=false continues into CPA and never calls persistFailed). OrchestratorServiceRetryHeaderTest 4/4 (unchanged, unaffected by refactor). OutboundMessageServiceRollbackTest 7/7 (Phase-1 regression – still green). ApplicationYamlSchemaPropertyTest 4/4, MessageStatusReconciliationSchedulerTest 3/3, OutboundSoapClientDynamicTrustTest 3/3, RawPayloadCaptureInterceptorTest 5/5, EbmsOrchestratorApplicationTests 1/1. The three Testcontainers-based integration tests (InboundPipelineIntegrationTest, OutboundPipelineIntegrationTest, OrchestratorServiceIntegrationTest) FAIL with the SAME environment error as iteration_25: IllegalStateException 'Previous attempts to find a Docker environment failed' — no Docker daemon in this sandbox. This is an environment limitation, not a code regression: all three test classes compile cleanly and are picked up by Surefire. Code review of OrchestratorService.java and the new InboundMessageTrackingService.java confirms the architectural fix matches the outbound phase-1 pattern: (1) @Transactional removed from processInboundMessage(); (2) three tracking methods each annotated @Transactional(propagation=REQUIRES_NEW) — persistReceived (idempotent upsert), markProcessing (with ifPresentOrElse warn-not-throw guard), persistFailed (idempotent upsert; builds a fresh FAILED entity when no row exists yet); (3) validateInboundOin & rejectSecurityFailure simplified — the latter now purely logs+throws EbmsException(SecurityFailure), with FAILED persistence + audit event centralised in the catch blocks of processInboundMessage(); (4) DuplicateMessageException caught first with a dedicated no-op branch (persistDuplicate already ran, original row intentionally untouched); (5) catch(EbmsException) and catch(Exception) both call trackingService.persistFailed(...) + publishAudit(MESSAGE_REJECTED FAILURE) + rethrow — so all four rejection paths (OIN mismatch, CPA failure, decryption failure, signature verification failure) now leave a FAILED row with error_message populated, which was the bug being fixed. InboundPipelineIntegrationTest.java contains the two required renamed tests (processInboundMessage_invalidSignature_persistsAsFailed, processInboundMessage_cpaValidationFails_persistsAsFailedWithoutCrypto) plus the 7 unchanged tests — all 9 compile.
action_items: InboundPipelineIntegrationTest (Testcontainers, needs Docker for postgres+rabbitmq) was NOT executed here — no Docker daemon in this Kubernetes sandbox (same limitation as iteration_25 phase-1). Please run it locally / in CI with Docker to fully validate the 9 pipeline scenarios, in particular the two updated tests processInboundMessage_invalidSignature_persistsAsFailed and processInboundMessage_cpaValidationFails_persistsAsFailedWithoutCrypto that assert the new FAILED-row behavior end-to-end (including a real JPA commit surviving the outer exception).

Optional: consider making buildEntity() a bit more defensive when header.getFrom()/getTo() lists are empty (currently falls back to clientOin for from and null for to — acceptable for the FAILED path, but a totally-empty header on persistFailed could still write UNKNOWNs; same informational point raised in iteration_25 for the outbound side).
critical_code_review_comments: Correct architectural fix: OrchestratorService.processInboundMessage() no longer @Transactional; all inbound persistence delegated to InboundMessageTrackingService with Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW on all three methods — guarantees FAILED/RECEIVED/PROCESSING rows commit independently of the outer flow that rethrows.

Ordering of catches is right: catch(DuplicateMessageException) precedes catch(EbmsException e) — since DuplicateMessageException extends EbmsException, this prevents a redundant persistFailed() on duplicate submissions (original row is intentionally untouched, only an audit MESSAGE_DUPLICATE was published inline).

persistFailed() is idempotent via findByMessageId(messageId).map(...).orElseGet(...) — safe if a prior partial run had already persisted a PROCESSING row for the same messageId; it correctly transitions the existing row to FAILED with errorMessage.
persistFailed() short-circuits with a WARN log (no exception) when header.getMessageInfo() is null or messageId is blank, which prevents a double-fault when the header itself is malformed.

Simplified validateInboundOin/rejectSecurityFailure signatures (3/2 params) — the old inline messageRepository.save()/publishAudit() are gone; all rejection persistence flows through the unified catch block, which eliminates the previous silent-rollback bug.

Informational (not blocking): in catch(Exception e) the persisted errorMessage is exceptionClassName+': '+e.getMessage(); when e.getMessage() is null the placeholder '<geen detail>' is used — good, matches outbound-phase pattern.

Informational: buildEntity() sets fromPartyId to clientOin when header.getFrom() is empty — reasonable fallback so the FAILED row still shows the actor identity from the mTLS-verified gateway header rather than null.

rca of the issue: Original inbound bug (mirror of iteration_25 outbound): OrchestratorService.processInboundMessage() was annotated @Transactional at method scope. Any exception on the 4 rejection paths (OIN antispoofing mismatch, CPA validation failure, cryptoServiceClient.decrypt() failure, cryptoServiceClient.verify() failure) triggered Spring's default rollback of the whole transaction. The old rejectSecurityFailure() branch DID call messageRepository.save() to persist a FAILED row inline, but that save participated in the same enclosing transaction and got rolled back by the same exception it was trying to record — so failed inbound messages left ZERO trace in ebms_message/the admin UI. Fix: extract all inbound DB writes into InboundMessageTrackingService (three methods, each Propagation.REQUIRES_NEW: persistReceived, markProcessing, persistFailed — all idempotent upserts by messageId). processInboundMessage() is no longer transactional and is wrapped in try/catch(DuplicateMessageException)/catch(EbmsException)/catch(Exception). On EbmsException and generic Exception, trackingService.persistFailed(header, rawSoap, clientOin, errorDetail) commits status=FAILED with error_message in its own transaction that survives the outer rethrow. DuplicateMessageException is caught first (before the generic EbmsException catch) so duplicate submissions don't overwrite the original row.
